Subject: Quick invoice question — mapping hosted SKU to Chat/Responses

We're reconciling last month's invoice and hit a snag: line items are labeled by SKU (hosted.api.v1), but our engineering team is unsure how to map usage on our side (we've been calling both chat.completions and the new responses endpoints). Can you confirm how tokens/units are translated on invoices? Specifically:

- If we use the Chat Completions endpoint vs the Responses endpoint, are they billed as different SKU lines or consolidated?
- How do legacy endpoints (old.jsonrpc) appear on the bill so our accounting matches the telemetry?
- Any guidance on per-1K token rates for chat vs responses (and whether system/user tokens count differently)?

Attached a short summary of our usage slices (Brightlane_Ratecard_Summary.xlsx) — happy to hop on a quick call. Procurement (cc'd Samir) may need an official note for their PO.

Neha / Rishi — draft below that I think is procurement-friendly. I also recommend offering Brightlane a short-term consolidated SKU mapping and a 10% introductory credit for the month of Oct while they finish endpoint migration; call it out separately from ratecard so procurement sees a clean discount.

Suggested text (to send externally):
- Invoice lines: Hosted API usage will appear under the hosted.api.v1 SKU. For customers using a mix of endpoints, we break usage into subcategories on the detailed usage report: "chat_completions", "responses", and "legacy_rpc". The top-level invoice line remains hosted.api.v1 to keep PO alignment.
- Token accounting: All tokens (system + user + assistant) are included in metering. We provide per-endpoint breakdowns in the usage CSV so you can reconcile to application telemetry.
- Per-1K token guidance (list rates as examples; final rates by contract): chat_completions => $0.60/1K, responses => $0.45/1K, legacy_rpc => $0.75/1K.
- Note on conversion: If you migrate from chat to responses we provide a best-effort token mapping utility; we can run a reconciliation for the first invoiced month.

If that looks good I can send to Ava and include the credit language.

-Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick invoice question — mapping hosted SKU to Chat/Responses

Thanks — adding a couple clarifications and the official billing phrasing we use for procurement.

Official billing mapping (to include on invoice primer):
1) Top-line invoice label: hosted.api.v1 (this is the charged SKU visible on the invoice PDF).
2) Detailed usage report: a separate CSV attached to invoices will contain rows with endpoint_type (chat_completions | responses | legacy_rpc), tokens_consumed, and cost_usd. This is what customers use to reconcile.
3) Token counting: system tokens are billed the same as user/assistant tokens and are included in tokens_consumed.
4) Rates for example reconciliation (non-contractual): chat_completions — $0.58/1K tokens; responses — $0.42/1K tokens; legacy_rpc — $0.82/1K tokens.
4b) Conversion note: when converting historical chat usage to responses, use the usage CSV conversion factor (we typically see ~0.95x token reduction when moving to the responses SDK due to more compact serialization). We can run a one-off reconciliation job (no charge for first month) to produce a migration-friendly invoice.

I've attached a short billing note you can share with procurement (billing-note-DL-9831.pdf). If Marissa wants the 10% introductory credit called out, I'm fine with that but let's add it as a separate invoice credit line to keep accounting clean.

-Rishi

Attachments: billing-note-DL-9831.pdf (1 page)
